name: OFAC Framework for Compliance Commitments — Sanctions Compliance Program
reference: OFAC Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments (May 2019)
supervisor: OFAC — US Department of the Treasury

articles.title: Senior-management review + approval
articles.requirement: Senior management (board / equivalent) reviews + approves the sanctions compliance program (SCP) at inception + on material change; demonstrates ownership through written commitment + governance involvement; SCP integrated into the institution's broader compliance + risk-management framework.

articles.title: Sanctions compliance officer + resources
articles.requirement: A compliance officer is appointed with sufficient authority + autonomy + qualifications + access to senior management. Adequate resources allocated to the SCP: budget for technology + staff + training + auditing; the SCP is not under-resourced relative to the institution's risk profile.

articles.title: Culture of compliance
articles.requirement: Senior management promotes a culture of compliance — through internal communications, performance metrics, recognition + escalation channels free from retaliation. Avoids any messaging that suggests sanctions compliance is subordinate to business objectives.

articles.title: Documented sanctions risk assessment
articles.requirement: Documented assessment of the institution's sanctions exposure: customer / counterparty risk (jurisdictions of origin / residence, sanctions screening hits, beneficial-ownership exposure); product + service risk (correspondent banking, trade finance, payment processing, crypto); geographic risk (sanctioned + adjacent jurisdictions, transit countries); delivery-channel risk (face-to-face vs remote, intermediaries); transaction risk (single vs structured, frequency, value).

articles.title: Refresh cadence + triggers
articles.requirement: Risk assessment refreshed periodically (at least annually) + on material change: new business line, M&A, regulatory change (new sanctions regime / new designations), detected red flag or breach. Updates flow through to internal-controls calibration + training + screening-system tuning.

articles.title: Written policies + procedures
articles.requirement: Written policies + procedures operationalising the SCP: governance + accountability; screening (onboarding + ongoing + transaction); 50% Rule + beneficial-ownership attribution; escalation + decision authority; record-keeping (5+ years; now 10 years per NDAA 2024 SoL extension); license-management; secondary-sanctions analysis; integration with customer due diligence.

articles.title: Technological solutions — screening + filtering
articles.requirement: Sanctions screening systems calibrated to the institution's risk profile: list coverage (OFAC SDN + Non-SDN + sectoral; UK + EU + UN; local national lists); matching logic (fuzzy + transliteration + alias + script-conversion); ongoing list updates (real-time / daily); false-positive + false-negative tuning; alert workflow + decision audit trail.

articles.title: Lines of responsibility + accountability
articles.requirement: Clear allocation of responsibility for SCP execution: who screens, who investigates alerts, who decides on alerts, who escalates, who reports to senior management. First-line + second-line + internal-audit responsibilities differentiated. Documented escalation paths for alerts + apparent violations.

articles.title: Comprehensive + independent + objective testing
articles.requirement: Periodic testing + auditing of the SCP by qualified + independent (internal-audit or external) party. Scope: governance, risk assessment, policies + procedures, screening-system tuning + alert-workflow effectiveness, training programme. Identifies deficiencies; remediation tracked through to closure.

articles.title: Screening-system testing
articles.requirement: Specific testing of sanctions-screening systems: false-positive analysis (effective tuning); false-negative analysis (designated entries reaching the system that should be matched); alert disposition quality; sample-based reperformance of compliance decisions; technology change-management testing on configuration updates.

articles.title: Role-specific training
articles.requirement: Periodic + role-specific training: front-line (red flags, escalation); compliance staff (regime detail, current designations, screening-system); senior management (governance + accountability + program status); board (overview + key risks). Training content reflects current regimes + emerging risks + lessons-learned from incidents.

articles.title: Documentation + acknowledgement
articles.requirement: Training completion tracked + recorded; staff acknowledgement of training receipt + understanding; refresher cycle (typically annual at minimum); content updated for regime changes + emerging typologies; testing of staff knowledge through assessments or scenario exercises.

articles.title: Root-cause analysis on apparent violations
articles.requirement: On any apparent violation: prompt root-cause analysis identifying the specific failure (controls, technology, training, governance); remediation plan addressing the root cause (not just the symptom); evaluation of related risks for similar exposures elsewhere in the institution; documentation suitable for sharing with OFAC in a Voluntary Self-Disclosure or response to administrative subpoena.

articles.title: Mitigating factors in OFAC enforcement
articles.requirement: OFAC's published Enforcement Guidelines identify factors that mitigate penalties: existence of an effective SCP at the time of the violation (CFCC compliance); prompt voluntary self-disclosure; comprehensive cooperation; substantive remedial measures; the absence of similar past violations within the relevant SoL period (now 10 years). Strong programs reduce penalty exposure by 50%+.
